objects.original: The smooth normalized log-density ratio of the restricted-Gaussian fiber centered at y relative to the fiber centered at y'.
objects.reconstructed: The displayed function q_y-log Z_y-q_y'+log Z_y', differentiated by the real Hilbert-space gradient.
objects.evidence: The theorem displays the function; the private quadraticExponent is exactly -norm(t-y)^2/(2 eta), and no canonical llr is differentiated.

domains.original: Euclidean restricted-Gaussian fibers with eta>0 and normalized laws.
domains.reconstructed: Any complete real inner-product space, nonzero eta, arbitrary measurable structure and base measure.
domains.evidence: Only Hilbert-space calculus and spatial constancy are used; the lesson restricts the probability interpretation to the source-valid positive-eta specialization.

quantifiers.original: Every pair of centers and every spatial point for an admissible eta.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Every nonzero eta and all y, y' and x.
quantifiers.evidence: On eta>0 the quantifiers coincide; negative eta only extends the algebraic calculus identity.

assumptions.original: Positive eta and a normalized restricted-Gaussian setting.
assumptions.reconstructed: Nonzero eta and complete real inner-product structure, without normalization or integrability assumptions.
assumptions.evidence: The normalizer terms are spatial constants, so the bare derivative theorem needs no probability interpretation.

conclusion.original: The spatial gradient is eta inverse times y-y'.
conclusion.reconstructed: gradient of the displayed representative at x equals eta^-1 • (y-y').
conclusion.evidence: The two quadratic gradients subtract with the exact center order and coefficient.

scopes.original: Only the smooth score calculation, excluding Fisher, LSI, Talagrand and Wasserstein conclusions.
scopes.reconstructed: A genuine derivative identity for the displayed function, with no canonical-llr derivative or functional inequality.
scopes.evidence: The private helper proves HasFDerivAt and the public theorem never differentiates the a.e. llr identity.

constant_dependencies.original: The normalizers depend on the base, eta and centers but not x; the score depends only on eta and y-y'.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The factor two cancels and both normalizer derivatives vanish.

deltas.description: The calculus theorem extends positive eta in Euclidean space to nonzero eta in a complete real inner-product space.
The standalone derivative identity permits arbitrary base measures and total real integral/log constants, while its normalized-density interpretation remains restricted to admissible fibers.

review_evidence: Fresh packet-only review included the exact whole module and lesson, checked the private norm-square derivative and public cancellation proof, and found no blocking mathematical or publication-context delta. A reviewer-issued schema-only amendment records the two benign source-specializing generalizations as explicit elaborations; substantive findings are unchanged.
